newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares pause again, focus on lesser-knowns.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares pause again, focus on lesser-knowns.

text.p: Russian shares slipped slightly on Tuesday in light trading as investors paused yet again to take a breather from recent heady gains, traders and dealers said.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index edged down to close at 327.35 from 329.48 on Monday on total volume of $28 million.
"Investors wanted to see the market cool down, and certainly a cooling down was necessary," said Andrei Ippolitov, head of trading at Prospect.

Andrei Galperin of Creditansalt Grant said the market was shifting its attention to secondary shares from leading paper and forecast a downward price trend for top shares in coming weeks as investors look at lesser-known companies.
"There is a serious imbalance in the market between leading shares and second- and third-tiers," he said.
"At these prices, Russia's best stocks will be bought only if there is a rush. Now investors will buy only what is cheaper."

Traders said a winning bid for 40.12 percent of oil major Surgut Holding (NK Surgutneftegaz) by pension-fund manager ZAO Surgutfondinvest had little effect on the company's price, with Surgut ordinaries closing unchanged from Monday's $0.75.
Shares in Moscow electricity company Mosenergo ticked up to $1.445 from $1.435.
Oil company Lukoil edged down to $15.15 from $15.25 and national electricity utility Unified Energy System, or UES, also known as United Energy, slipped slightly to $0.2301 from $0.2320.
The Russian market has spent this week cooling down after heady gains in the previous week and a string of record-setting closes and volumes.

News on Tuesday that the International Monetary Fund had put on the brakes in its dealings with Russia and said payment of part of a $10 billion loan was not yet likely had not affected the market, dealers said.

"Everybody knows that they didn't give out the money today, but that tomorrow they will," said Galperin, adding that the delay might spook Western investors slightly but that Russian buyers were not concerned.
